questions.question: 70. Buna-S can be represented as:
questions.explanation:
Buna-S is a synthetic rubber which is a copolymer of 1,3-butadiene and styrene. The name is derived from: 'Bu' for butadiene, 'na' for sodium (the catalyst originally used), and 'S' for styrene. It is formed by addition polymerization.

In this reaction, 1,3-butadiene undergoes 1,4-addition, forming a `-CH₂-CH=CH-CH₂-` unit. This unit then links with the styrene monomer unit `-CH(C₆H₅)-CH₂-`. The resulting polymer chain has the repeating unit shown in option (2).

questions.question: Caprolactam when heated at high temperature in presence of water, gives
questions.explanation:
Caprolactam undergoes ring-opening polymerization when heated at high temperature in the presence of water. This reaction yields Nylon 6.

Nylon 6 is a polyamide formed from a single monomer, caprolactam. The number '6' indicates that the monomer caprolactam contains six carbon atoms.

questions.question: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Ethene at 333 to 343 K and 6-7 atm pressure in the presence of $AlEt_{3}$ and $TiCl_{4}$ undergoes addition polymerization to give LDP. Statement II : Caprolactam at 533-543 K in $H_{2}O$ through step growth polymerizes to give Nylon 6. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.explanation:
(Fact-Based)

Statement-I : Ethene at 333 to 343 K and 6-7 atm pressure of \(AlEt_{3}\) and \(TiCl_{4}\) undergo addition polymerization to give HDPE not LDPE. Therefore, Statement I is false.

Statement-II :

Caprolactam undergoes ring-opening polymerization in the presence of water at high temperatures (533-543 K) to form Nylon 6. This is a type of step-growth polymerization. Therefore, Statement II is true.

Thus, Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.explanation:
(A) Glyptal is a polyester used in the manufacture of paints and lacquers. So, A matches with III.

(B) Neoprene is a synthetic rubber which is resistant to vegetable and mineral oils. It is used for making gaskets. So, B matches with IV.

(C) Acrilan (or Orlon) is polyacrylonitrile, which is used as a substitute for wool in making commercial fibres. So, C matches with II.

(D) LDP (Low-Density Polyethene) is chemically inert and tough but flexible. It is used in the insulation of electricity-carrying wires and in the manufacture of squeeze bottles, toys and flexible pipes. So, D matches with I.

The correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

questions.question: On complete hydrogenation, natural rubber produces
questions.explanation:
### Detailed Solution

Natural rubber (NR) is cis-1,4-polyisoprene. Its repeating unit contains one double bond. Complete hydrogenation involves the addition of hydrogen across this double bond, saturating it.
The repeating unit of the hydrogenated natural rubber is \(-\text{CH}_{2}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_{3})-\text{CH}_{2}-\text{CH}_{2}-\). This structure is equivalent to a copolymer formed from the polymerization of ethylene (\(\text{CH}_{2}=\text{CH}_{2}\)) and propylene (\(\text{CH}_{2}=\text{CH}(\text{CH}_{3})\)) units.
Thus, on complete hydrogenation, natural rubber produces an ethylene-propylene copolymer.

questions.question: In the following reaction sequence, major products X and Y are acyclic monomers. 500 mol of X completely reacts with 500 mol of Y to give 1 mol of a single biodegradable acyclic copolymer Z as the only product. The amount of Z formed in grams is $ \_\_\_\_\_ $. Given: • Atomic mass (in amu): H: 1, C: 12, N: 14, O: 16, Br : 80
questions.explanation:
### Step 1: Determine the structure of X


### Step 2: Determine the structure of Y

Caprolactam undergoes hydrolysis in the presence of \(H_{3}O^{+}\) to form 6-aminohexanoic acid (Y).
$$
\text{Caprolactam} \xrightarrow{H_{3}O^{+}, \Delta} HO-C-(CH_{2})_{5}-NH_{2} \quad (Y)
$$

### Step 3: Polymerization of X and Y to form Z

X is glycine (\(NH_{2}-CH_{2}-COOH\)) and Y is 6-aminohexanoic acid (\(HOOC-(CH_{2})_{5}-NH_{2}\)). These react to form a copolymer Z.
(500 \text{ mole}) \quad NH_{2}-CH_{2}-COOH \quad + \quad HOOC-(CH_{2})_{5}-NH_{2} \quad (500 \text{ mole})
$$
\downarrow -999 H_{2}O
$$

### Step 4: Calculate the molar mass of Z

The copolymer Z is formed from 500 moles of X and 500 moles of Y, resulting in 1 mole of copolymer Z. The repeating unit of Z is \([-NH-CH_{2}-CO-NH-(CH_{2})_{5}-CO-]\).
$$
Molar mass of repeating unit from X (glycine residue): \(CH_{2}CO\) is \(12+2(1)+12+2(16) = 12+2+12+32 = 58\).
$$
$$
Molar mass of repeating unit from Y (6-aminohexanoic acid residue): \((CH_{2})_{5}CO\) is \(5(12)+10(1)+12+16 = 60+10+12+16 = 98\).
$$
$$
Molar mass of \(NH\) group: \(14+1 = 15\).
$$
Molar mass of one repeating unit of Z (from one X and one Y, minus 2 water molecules):
$$
M_{X} = 2C + 3H + N + 2O = 2(12) + 3(1) + 14 + 2(16) = 24 + 3 + 14 + 32 = 73 \text{ g/mol}
$$
$$
M_{Y} = 6C + 13H + N + 2O = 6(12) + 13(1) + 14 + 2(16) = 72 + 13 + 14 + 32 = 131 \text{ g/mol}
$$
When X and Y polymerize, they form amide linkages, eliminating water. The repeating unit of the copolymer Z is \([-NH-CH_{2}-CO-NH-(CH_{2})_{5}-CO-]\).
Molar mass of one repeating unit (from X and Y combined, minus 2 water molecules for each pair):
$$
\text{Molar mass of } X = 75 \text{ g/mol (Glycine)}
$$
$$
\text{Molar mass of } Y = 131 \text{ g/mol (6-aminohexanoic acid)}
$$
The repeating unit of the copolymer is formed by the condensation of one molecule of X and one molecule of Y, with the loss of two water molecules. So, the molar mass of one repeating unit is \(M_{X} + M_{Y} - 2 \times M_{H_{2}O}\).
$$
\text{Molar mass of repeating unit} = (75 + 131) - 2(18) = 206 - 36 = 170 \text{ g/mol}
$$
Since 500 mol of X and 500 mol of Y react to give 1 mol of copolymer Z, the copolymer Z contains 500 repeating units. The structure shown in the solution indicates 500 repeating units, with an \(H\) at one end and an \(OH\) at the other end.
The molar mass of Z is \(500 \times (\text{Molar mass of repeating unit}) + \text{Molar mass of end groups}\).
The molar mass of the repeating unit \([-NH-CH_{2}-CO-NH-(CH_{2})_{5}-CO-]\) is \(170\) g/mol.
The end groups are \(H-\)(from \(NH_{2}\) of first unit) and \(-OH\) (from \(COOH\) of last unit). So, the total mass of end groups is \(1 + 17 = 18\) g/mol.
$$
\text{Total mass of Z} = (\text{Molar mass of repeating unit} \times 500) + \text{Molar mass of end groups}
$$
$$
= 170 \times 500 + 18
$$
$$
= 85000 + 18
$$
$$
= 85018
$$
The amount of Z formed in grams is 85018.
